verdict.rationale: mise has no built-in natural-language command interface of its own. It does ship a first-party `mise mcp` server that lets an AI assistant read a project's tools, tasks, env vars and config and run its tasks, so a user can operate mise conversationally through an external assistant. The documented scope is limited to inspecting and running tasks. Missing for 10: native natural-language command parsing in mise itself, documented NL control of tool installs, version changes and bootstrap, and independent or hands-on corroboration of the MCP workflow.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can operate the product with natural-language commands

citations.quote: `mise mcp` runs a Model Context Protocol server that lets an AI assistant read a project's tools, tasks, environment variables and config files, and run its tasks.
The mise MCP server lets an AI assistant inspect a project's tools, tasks, environment, and configuration, and run mise tasks.
